curation.why: The Settings frame displays the signed-in account at the top of the card, in large legible type. CI captures signed in as the end-to-end test account, so the frame read `subly-e2e+1785856022717@nikatru.com` — an internal test address on a public marketing asset. Removed rather than published.
curation.whyNotRecaptured: Re-running the workflow reproduces it: the capture signs in as that same account, so ANY frame showing the account card carries the address. This is a defect in the capture, not in the curation, and it is recorded as such in the directory README.
curation.costOfRemoval: None. tooling/channel-register.json sets minCount 2 and recommendedCount 4; four frames satisfy both.

🔴 whyThisBlockExists: assert-listing-assets.mjs compares this count to the bytes beside it, precisely so a removed frame cannot leave provenance describing a set that is no longer here. Editing `count` to 4 alone would have satisfied that check while making this file claim a four-frame capture run that never happened — provenance that passes and lies. The run produced five; four are published; both numbers are stated.
